c.tagline: Saint-Martin's French-side capital — a fort-topped harbor town of Creole markets, marina cafes, and gourmet cuisine.

taxi.fareNote: No Uber or ride-hailing. Taxis charge fixed government-set fares by zone, with surcharges after dark and on Sundays; confirm the fare before departing.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number reaching police, fire, and ambulance; on the French side dial 17 for police and 15 for medical.

avoid.reason: Car break-ins at beach parking lots and theft of items left on the sand are the main risks; avoid deserted beaches and unlit streets after dark.

hood_desc: Marigot's walkable heart — Rue de la République's Creole shopfronts and the West Indies Mall, the open-air waterfront market, hilltop Fort Louis (1789), and the Port La Royale marina ringed with French bistros; the convenient sightseeing-and-dining base.
A slim beach isthmus just west of town with the open sea on one side and the Simpson Bay Lagoon on the other, lined with mid-range resort hotels minutes from Marigot; quiet and beach-focused.

A laid-back beach village north of town, the island's self-styled 'gourmet capital,' with one beachfront street of acclaimed restaurants and casual 'lolo' barbecue grills; relaxed by day, foodie by night.
A sheltered cove and yacht marina tucked into the forested northern tip, home to secluded resort hotels; the calmest, most private base, about 15 minutes from Marigot.
The island's liveliest beach, a two-kilometre arc of white sand backed by beach bars, watersports, and a low-key village; sun-and-sea days with a party edge, on the northeast coast.

water.note: Desalinated tap water is safe, though many prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: Shared minibuses run mainly in daylight (roughly 6 AM to 6-7 PM) and thin out on Sundays; after dark you rely on taxis.
transit.note: Saint-Martin has no rail. Getting around is by shared minibus vans, taxis, or rental car. Marigot's waterfront is the ferry hub for Anguilla (Blowing Point) and boats to Saint-Barthélemy and Pinel Island.
transit.pay: Shared minibus vans display their route and cost about €1-2, paid in cash to the driver; flag one down anywhere along the route. There is no transit card. Taxis charge fixed government-set fares by zone.

bus: Public minibuses (shared vans) across the French side and to Philipsburg

landmarks: Fort Louis
A short climb to this 1789 French hilltop fort earns sweeping views over Marigot Bay, Simpson Bay Lagoon and neighboring Anguilla.
Marigot Market
The waterfront market bursts with spices, tropical fruit, fresh-caught snapper and Creole craftwork beneath cheerful red-roofed stalls.
Marina Royale
A yacht-lined French Riviera-style basin ringed with bistros and boutiques, perfect for sunset rosé and people-watching à la française.
Rue de la République
Marigot's main street preserves gingerbread-trimmed Creole townhouses housing patisseries and boutiques, the essence of French Caribbean charm.
Pic Paradis
Saint-Martin's highest point at 424 meters, its rainforest trails and lookouts survey both the French and Dutch sides of the island.
Loterie Farm
A former sugar plantation turned hillside eco-hideaway with ziplines, forest hikes and a famously stylish spring-fed pool lounge.
Grand Case
The island's gourmet village, a beachfront strip where lolos grill barbecue beside acclaimed French restaurants along a photogenic crescent bay.
Friar's Bay Beach
A tranquil family cove between Marigot and Grand Case, its calm turquoise water framed by beach bars and green headlands.
Baie Rouge
A wild, russet-sand beach in the Terres Basses where dramatic surf, cliffs and the David's Hole rock arch invite explorers.
Catholic Church of Marigot
A simple, cheerful 1841 stone-and-timber parish church whose bell tower and pastel interior anchor old Marigot's spiritual life.

train.note: There is no railway on Saint-Martin or anywhere in the French Antilles' Leeward islands. Arrive by air into Princess Juliana on the Dutch side or the small Grand Case airport, or by ferry from neighbouring islands.

intl.to: Philipsburg & Simpson Bay (Sint Maarten, Netherlands) - across the open island border
intl.op: local minibus operators — pay the driver

bus.note: The border between the French and Dutch halves is open with no checkpoint, so minibuses run between Marigot and Philipsburg as ordinary local services - a few euros or dollars paid to the driver. They run frequently in daylight and stop early in the evening. There is no formal terminal; buses pick up along the main roads.

intl.to: Anguilla - Blowing Point (UK) - from Marigot, ~25 min

ferry.note: Marigot's waterfront terminal handles the main crossing to Anguilla, which runs roughly every 45 minutes through the day and takes 25 minutes - immigration is cleared at both ends, so carry your passport. The Voyager fast ferry to St Barth also leaves from here. Sailings are cancelled in heavy swell, which is common in the winter months.

half.name: Anguilla
half.blurb: A British island reached by a thirty-minute public ferry, known for the white sand and turquoise water of Shoal Bay.

half.name: Saint-Barthélemy
half.blurb: A French island about an hour away by ferry with upscale beaches and the harbor town of Gustavia.
